scope: Proposition 6.5 (Exact full-period transmission) of the manuscript “A counterexample to integer-degree harmonic dimension comparison” (preprints/A-counterexample-to-integer-degree-harmonic-dimension-comparison-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 361 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c6adbdbf2331bf0f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 28. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For finite spectral data as specified at the end of Section 3, choose the word and compact pulse family above. There are a starting index j0 and parameters hj ∈ K, for every j ≥ j0, such that the center-regular value transmissions of the resulting metric satisfy Tl,j = sl,jDl,jΠl, sl,j > 0, | log sl,j| ≤ CTj (2 ≤ l ≤ L, j ≥ j0). (6.26) The positive diagonal matrices Dl,j propagate the reference Cauchy data (I, θlI) over the entire leg following the pulse; they satisfy (6.25). The regular value equation has the bounds (6.9). All estimates used to choose j0 are uniform over preceding admitted controls for this fixed finite family.
